## First finding as a plain-language heading

<!-- One or two paragraphs, then one chart. -->

::: panel-tabset
### Mother tongue is not English or French

```{r}
#| label: language-other
#| output: asis

# The two measures, one to a tab. The second is a share of a share - German or
# Pennsylvania German among those whose mother tongue is neither English nor
# French. Both are percentages, but of different denominators, so each chart
# keeps its own scale.

# Roughly how many characters of label fit across a chart at this font size on
# a phone, read off a render. Used below to decide which labels fit inside
# their bars.
panel_chars_wide <- 45

language_bars_data <- language |>
  # One order for both tabs, set on the first, so a place stays on the same row
  # when the reader switches tabs and only its bar changes length.
  mutate(district = fct_reorder(district, non_official_percent)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(non_official_percent, german_percent_of_non_official),
    names_to = "measure", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(label = label_number(accuracy = 1, suffix = "%")(value)) |>
  # Whether a label fits inside its bar, asked for each measure on its own
  # because each chart has its own scale. The axis runs to about 1.2 times the
  # longest bar, and one character is 1 / panel_chars_wide of that; a label
  # needs its length plus a space or so of padding.
  mutate(
    inside = value >= (nchar(label) + 1.5) * (max(value) * 1.2 / panel_chars_wide),
    .by = measure
  )

# Both tabs draw the same chart from a different measure, so it is built once
# here. Titles, subtitles and captions differ, so each tab adds its own labs().
language_bars <- function(which) {
  bars <- language_bars_data |> filter(measure == which)

  ggplot(bars, aes(x = value, y = district, fill = district_type)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    # The baseline the bars grow from; theme_cwr()'s own x axis line is switched
    # off below, because with labels on the bars there is no axis to carry.
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = label,
        # Inside the bar end, or just past it
        hjust = if_else(inside, 1.15, -0.15),
        # White inside the dark city bars only; inside the light township
        # bars, and outside any bar, black reads better
        colour = if_else(inside & district_type == "City", "white", "black")
      ),
      size = label_size * 0.8
    ) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(City = dodgerblue, Township = dodgerblue50),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    # Room on the right for any label that sits outside its bar
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20))) +
    # The house short form of a long municipal name
    scale_y_discrete(labels = cwr_short_name) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    # Every bar carries its number, so the value axis and its gridlines are gone.
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )
}

# Alt text read top to bottom, in the order the rows are drawn
language_alt <- function(which) {
  language_bars_data |>
    filter(measure == which) |>
    arrange(desc(district)) |>
    summarise(entries = paste(paste0(district, " ", label), collapse = ", ")) |>
    pull(entries)
}

# Said once, in both tabs' captions
mother_tongue_note <- "Mother tongue is the language first learned at home in childhood and still understood"

p <- language_bars("non_official_percent") +
  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when",
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Statistics Canada Table 98-10-0180-01",
      credit = TRUE,
      notes = mother_tongue_note
    )
  )

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-language-other",
  alt = paste0(
    "Horizontal bars, one row per municipality, showing the percentage of ",
    "people whose mother tongue is neither English nor French, highest at the ",
    "top, with the three cities in dark blue and the four townships in light blue. ",
    language_alt("non_official_percent"), "."
  )
  # No height given: cwr_figure() sets it from the number of rows.
)
```

### Is German or Pennsylvania German

```{r}
#| label: language-german
#| output: asis

p <- language_bars("german_percent_of_non_official") +
  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when",
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Statistics Canada Table 98-10-0180-01",
      credit = TRUE,
      notes = c(mother_tongue_note, "German and Pennsylvania German counted together")
    )
  )

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-language-german",
  alt = paste0(
    "Horizontal bars, one row per municipality, showing the percentage of ",
    "people with a mother tongue other than English or French whose mother ",
    "tongue is German or Pennsylvania German. Rows are in the same order as the ",
    "previous tab, not by these figures. The three cities are in dark blue and the ",
    "four townships in light blue. ",
    language_alt("german_percent_of_non_official"), "."
  )
  # No height given: cwr_figure() sets it from the number of rows.
)
```
:::
